subtitle: When Banavasi Fell Silent and Badami Awoke

panels.shot: epic split-panel wide, one half showing fading Kadamba lion banner over Banavasi, the other half rising Chalukya standard over rugged Badami cliffs
panels.action: Harivarma & Krishnavarma II stand back-to-back in stylised contrast, one before the forested halls of Banavasi, the other before the red sandstone heights of Badami, as a lion banner droops and another standard catches the wind.

dialogue.text: In the shadowed years around 543, as Kadamba Banavasi fell silent, a new house at Badami quietly seized their lion’s banner and stepped into the light.

i18n.hi: पाँच सौ तैंतालीस के साये में, जब कदम्ब बनवासी सन्नाटे में डूबा, बदामी के नए घराने ने चुपचाप उनका सिंह ध्वज थाम लिया और रोशनी में आ गया।

panels.shot: slow push-in from sky over the Western Ghats down to the temple-town of Banavasi
panels.action: A misty dawn over dense Western Ghats opens to the tiled roofs and shrines of Banavasi, where Harivarma, older and thoughtful, looks out from a modest palace balcony toward the forested horizon.

dialogue.text: Once, Banavasi’s Kadambas had roared from forest to sea. By the time Harivarma’s copper plates were etched at Halasi, their roar had thinned into a guarded, regional voice.

i18n.hi: कभी बनवासी के कदम्ब जंगल से समंदर तक दहाड़ते थे। हलसी में हरिवर्मा की ताम्रपट्ट लिखे जाते-जाते, उनकी दहाड़ सिकुड़कर सतर्क, प्रांतीय सी आवाज रह गई।

panels.shot: medium close-up on an inscription being incised, with Harivarma in the background
panels.action: Inside a dim hall, a scribe bends over shining copper plates, stylus cutting precise Nagari lines as Harivarma, in simple but regal dress, watches with a grave, inward gaze.

dialogue.text: The Halasi plates call him Harivarma, Manavya-gotra, Hariti-putra. The old formulas remain, but the grants are local, the circle of power smaller than in his forefathers’ day.

i18n.hi: हलसी के पट्ट उन्हें हरिवर्मा, मानव्य-गोत्र, हरिति-पुत्र कहते हैं। पुरानी उपाधियाँ तो वही हैं, पर दान बस स्थानीय, और शक्ति का घेरा पूर्वजों से कहीं छोटा।

panels.shot: wide map-like bird’s-eye showing shifting powers across northern Karnataka and the Deccan
panels.action: A painterly, map-like vista shows the forests and rivers of northern Karnataka, with small symbolic standards of Kadambas, Gangas, Pallavas and new banners stirring in the upper Krishna valley.

dialogue.text: Around him, the Deccan had changed. Old alliances had frayed, new chiefs had risen. To the north-east, an obscure Chalukya house began to test its strength along the Malaprabha and upper Krishna.

i18n.hi: उधर पूरा दक्खिन बदल चुका था। पुराने मेल टूटे, नए सरदार उठे। उत्तर-पूर्व में एक अनजाना चालुक्य घराना मलप्रभा और ऊपरी कृष्णा के किनारे अपनी ताकत टटोलने लगा।

panels.shot: two-plane composition: foreground Harivarma in court, background faint silhouette of Krishnavarma II over Triparvatha hills
panels.action: Harivarma sits in a small court at Banavasi, counsellors close, as behind him a ghost-like overlay shows Krishnavarma II standing on a rocky Triparvatha hilltop, cloak caught in the wind.

dialogue.text: In the record, Harivarma is the last clear voice of Banavasi. Yet, in the rugged country of Triparvatha, another Kadamba, Krishnavarma II, stirred, carrying the same lineage crest into harsher hills.

i18n.hi: लेखों में हरिवर्मा बनवासी की आखिरी साफ आवाज है। पर त्रिपर्वत के उबड़-खाबड़ देश में एक और कदम्ब, कृष्णवर्मा द्वितीय, जगा, वही कुलचिह्न लेकर और भी कठोर पहाड़ियों में।

panels.shot: medium shot of Krishnavarma II with a small retinue, overlooking Triparvatha stronghold
panels.action: Krishnavarma II stands with a compact retinue of mailed warriors and standard-bearers on a rocky ridge, gazing down at a fortified hill-settlement, his face set with quiet resolve.

dialogue.text: Later tradition remembered Krishnavarma II as the Triparvatha lord who briefly drew scattered Kadamba strands together again, a last attempt to weave a single lion banner over their hills.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा उसे त्रिपर्वत का स्वामी याद करती है, जिसने बिखरे कदम्ब धागों को फिर एक बार समेटा, मानो पहाड़ियों पर एक आखिरी साझा सिंह ध्वज बुनने की कोशिश हो।

panels.shot: intercut composition: half-frame showing a modest Kadamba muster, half-frame a growing Chalukya war-band
panels.action: On one side, Harivarma reviews a relatively small line of spearmen and elephant or two in a clearing; opposite, a Chalukya chieftain’s growing war-band trains among red rocks, their numbers subtly larger.

dialogue.text: The Kadamba muster was no longer the broad levy of their prime. Meanwhile, the Chalukyas of the Manavya-gotra were gathering men and horses with a confidence that did not yet show in grand records.

i18n.hi: अब कदम्बों की फौज उनके उत्कर्ष जैसी चौड़ी जमात नहीं रही। उधर मानव्य-गोत्र के चालुक्य बेखटके आदमी-घोड़े जुटा रहे थे, ऐसा आत्मविश्वास जो अभी शिलालेखों में नहीं दिखता।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a temple ritual where both Harivarma and Krishnavarma II are evoked symbolically
panels.action: Priests in a village shrine offer fire and flowers before a lion-emblem pillar, as small painted panels on the wall show two Kadamba kings—one in a palace, one in a hill-fort—under the same ancestral symbol.

dialogue.text: Epigraphs do not narrate their private doubts. They only show us the public rites—the shared lion, the old gotra, the prayers that this fragile thread of royal fortune might hold.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख उनकी निजी हिचक नहीं सुनाते। वे तो बस राजकर्म दिखाते हैं—साझा सिंह, पुराना गोत्र, वही प्रार्थनाएँ कि राजसौभाग्य की यह नाज़ुक डोरी कहीं टूट न जाए।

panels.shot: intimate interior close shot, Harivarma in council with a single elder adviser
panels.action: By lamplight in a quiet Banavasi chamber, Harivarma leans forward on a low stool, brow furrowed, as an aged adviser kneels opposite, hands open in earnest counsel.

dialogue.speaker: harivarma_and_krishnavarma_ii
dialogue.text: If we cannot widen our circle, even our forests will slip away.

i18n.hi: अगर हम अपना घेरा न बढ़ाएँ, तो अपने जंगल भी हाथ से निकल जाएँगे।

panels.shot: wide shot of Krishnavarma II receiving emissaries under a makeshift canopy in the hills
panels.action: Under a cloth canopy on a windy plateau, Krishnavarma II hears emissaries from lowland chiefs; some kneel, others stand wary, all framed by the stark outline of Triparvatha’s slopes.

dialogue.text: From Moran and Kamath we infer only outlines: Triparvatha’s Krishnavarma II seems to have gathered these lesser powers, perhaps even brushing Banavasi itself, in a brief reunion of Kadamba strength.

i18n.hi: मोरान और कामत से हमें बस रेखाचित्र मिलते हैं: लगता है कि त्रिपर्वत का कृष्णवर्मा द्वितीय इन्हीं छोटे सरदारों को जुटा लाया, शायद बनवासी की चौखट तक, कदम्ब ताकत की एक झटपट वापसी में।

panels.shot: moody transitional wide shot of Banavasi palace darkening at dusk
panels.action: The Banavasi palace complex stands in deepening dusk; one wing is lit but much of it lies quiet, vines creeping near old walls, a lone guard silhouetted against the fading sky.

dialogue.text: Yet the sources fall silent on Harivarma’s end. No inscription tells of a terrible storm, a final battle, or a ritual abdication. Banavasi’s line simply fades from the copper and stone.

i18n.hi: पर स्रोत हरिवर्मा के अंत पर चुप हो जाते हैं। कोई लेख किसी भयानक तूफान, आखिरी युद्ध, या विधिवत त्याग का किस्सा नहीं सुनाता। बनवासी की वंशरेखा बस ताम्र और पत्थर से ओझल हो जाती है।

panels.shot: dynamic bird’s-eye of Badami cliffs, emphasizing the rugged landscape
panels.action: A sweeping bird’s-eye view reveals the dramatic, layered cliffs of Badami, with their rust-red faces, natural caves and a narrow valley where a small settlement clings to the waters below.

dialogue.text: Then, in 543, another voice cuts through the quiet. On the red cliffs of Badami, Mangalesha would later carve his boast, dating his inscription to Saka 465, declaring a Chalukya power already sure of itself.

i18n.hi: और फिर, पाँच सौ तैंतालीस में, एक और आवाज सन्नाटे को चीरती है। बदामी की लाल चट्टानों पर मंगलेश ने बाद में अपना गर्व उकेरा, शक ४६५ तिथि देकर, मानो चालुक्य शक्ति तब तक खुद पर पूरा भरोसा कर चुकी हो।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a Badami cave, Chalukya artisan carving the inscription
panels.action: Inside a newly cut cave shrine, a Chalukya artisan chisels steadily into the stone wall, while behind him priests prepare images and a nobleman watches with a calm, proprietorial air.

dialogue.text: That cave inscription names their house in the same Manavya-gotra, calls them Hariti-putra, as the Kadambas had once done. Was this shared blood, or deliberate borrowing of a fading prestige?

i18n.hi: उस गुफा लेख में उनका घराना भी मानव्य-गोत्र बताया, उन्हें भी हरिति-पुत्र कहा, जैसे कभी कदम्बों को कहते थे। यह साझा रक्त था, या ढलती शोभा का जानबूझकर उठाया हुआ श्रृंगार?

panels.shot: symbolic split: ghostly Harivarma and Krishnavarma II facing a rising, faceless Chalukya figure
panels.action: In a symbolic tableau, the faint, almost transparent figures of Harivarma and Krishnavarma II stand on one side, lion emblem dim beside them, while on the other a younger, faceless Chalukya ruler stands upright, hand on a new standard bearing a similar motif.

dialogue.text: Historians like Moraes and Kamath weigh the evidence carefully. They see a transition, not a sudden conquest: a Kadamba house losing height, a Chalukya house stepping onto a stage already prepared.

i18n.hi: मोरेस और कामत जैसे इतिहासकार साक्ष्य को तौलते हैं। उन्हें यह संक्रमण दिखता है, अचानक विजय नहीं—एक कदम्ब घराना ऊँचाई खोता हुआ, एक चालुक्य घराना पहले से सजे मंच पर कदम रखता हुआ।

panels.shot: low-angle shot from Badami valley looking up at cliffs, with faint overlay of Banavasi forests
panels.action: From the shadowed valley at Badami, the view rises to towering cliffs, and in the sky above, a faint overlay shows the canopy of Banavasi forests, as if the memory of one landscape hangs over another.

dialogue.text: Every new rock-cut shrine at Badami echoed older shrines in the Western Ghats. The Chalukyas ruled a wider plateau, but they walked paths first beaten by forest kings like the Kadambas.

i18n.hi: बदामी की हर नई शैल-मूर्ति में पश्चिमी घाट के पुराने देवालयों की गूँज थी। चालुक्य ऊँचे पठार के शासक थे, पर रास्ते वही थे, जो जंगल-राजा कदम्बों ने पहले कुचले थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of a village storyteller in later centuries narrating to an audience, with images of Harivarma, Krishnavarma II and Chalukyas painted behind
panels.action: Centuries later, in a village courtyard, a bard stands before a painted cloth showing Kadamba lions and Chalukya symbols, as villagers listen, faces lit by a small oil lamp.

dialogue.text: Later tales blurred lines. Some called the Chalukyas true heirs of Banavasi, others saw them as usurpers. The inscriptions themselves, plain in their dates and titles, offer no such drama.

i18n.hi: बाद की कथाओं ने रेखाएँ धुंधली कर दीं। कुछ ने चालुक्यों को बनवासी का सच्चा उत्तराधिकारी कहा, कुछ ने उन्हें हड़पने वाला। खुद शिलालेख, अपनी सीधी तिथियों और उपाधियों के साथ, ऐसा कोई नाटक नहीं रचते।

panels.shot: quiet close-up of an old Kadamba copper plate and a Chalukya stone inscription side by side
panels.action: On a scholar’s table, an aged copper plate of Harivarma lies beside a rubbing of the Badami cave inscription; a hand hovers above them, tracing the repeated words for gotra and goddess with a thoughtful finger.

dialogue.text: We see only overlapping words, shared formulas, the silence between dates. In that silence, Harivarma’s last grants and Krishnavarma’s brief reunion become the unseen bridge into the Chalukya age.

i18n.hi: हम बस मिलते-जुलते शब्द देखते हैं, साझा सूत्र, तारीखों के बीच की खामोशी। उसी खामोशी में हरिवर्मा की अंतिम दान-पट्ट और कृष्णवर्मा की क्षणिक एकता चालुक्य युग की अदृश्य पुल बन जाती है।

panels.shot: long temporal dissolve from early Banavasi forests to a distant glimpse of medieval Goa coast
panels.action: A gentle dissolve shifts from a dense Banavasi forest temple to, far in time, a glimpse of ships off a later medieval coast near Goa, their pennants fluttering above a seaside settlement.

dialogue.text: Much later, other Kadambas would rise by the sea at Gopakapattana, centuries after Banavasi fell and Badami rose. Their ocean winds carried only a faint echo of the old forest kings.

i18n.hi: बहुत बाद में, और कदम्ब सागर किनारे गोपकपट्टन पर उठे, सदियों बाद जब बनवासी ढला और बदामी उठा। उनकी समुद्री हवाओं में पुराने जंगल-राजाओं की बस हल्की-सी गूँज बची थी।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of an abandoned Banavasi hall with a lone lion emblem, light streaming in
panels.action: In an empty Banavasi audience hall, dust motes drift in a shaft of light; on a cracked pillar the Kadamba lion emblem still clings, weathered yet distinct, as if watching the centuries pass.

dialogue.text: Harivarma’s name and Krishnavarma’s hill-kingdom mark the last Kadamba dawn at Banavasi; their quiet fading reminds us that every fallen banner becomes the ground from which another empire climbs.

i18n.hi: हरिवर्मा का नाम और कृष्णवर्मा की पहाड़ी रियासत बनवासी की अंतिम कदम्ब सुबह को चिह्नित करते हैं; उनका शांत ढलान याद दिलाता है कि हर गिरा हुआ ध्वज वही ज़मीन बनता है, जहाँ से अगला साम्राज्य चढ़ता है।

title_i18n.en: The Lion Banner Passes to Badami

subtitle_i18n.en: When Banavasi Fell Silent and Badami Awoke
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब बनवासी चुप हुआ, बदामी जाग उठा
